newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end near highs after Dow recovery.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end near highs after Dow recovery.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.940 unch Gold NY 337.75 Lon fix 338.60
AUD US$0.7503 (Tue $0.7519) CRB Index cl 241.44 +0.19
*Stocks ended near highs and above 2,700 level after the Dow staged a big recovery on Tuesday. Total volume 360.0 million, value A$905.0 million, 1,211 stocks traded, 365 steady, 469 up, 377 down
Australian shares ended firmer and near their highs on Wednesday, the market climbing above the key 2,700 level after the Wall Street market staged an amazing recovery on Tuesday.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 16.7 points higher at 2,705.1 just 9.1 points short of its all-time record high of 2,714.2 set on June 20.
The June share price index ended up 17 points at 2,708 and at a 2.9 point premium to the underlying index.
The Dow industrials rose 154 points on Tuesday after falling 192 points on Monday on fears of higher interest rates.
"It was a little bit bouncy this morning but basically the market followed the Dow's trend," said Peter Struk, a dealer at Sydney broker, Reynolds & Co.
Struk said he saw evidence of offshore buying later in the session particularly for bank issues which augered well for trading on Thursday.
"The last couple of days before June 30 can be a bit messy because there is a lot of book squaring going with institutions locking in profits and losses for tax purposes," Struk said.
Struk said at this stage he was expecting to see a strong session for the end of Australia's financial year on June 30.
Industrials fared better than resources with a fall in copper and gold prices putting a cap on gains for most miners.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd continued to slide ahead of its annual results release on Friday and dealers said it and MIM Holdings were adversely affected by the weaker copper price.
BHP shares closed 15 cents weaker at A$19.25, while MIM shares ended five cents down at A$2.00.
Resource issues receiving the full benefit of better sentiment included Rio Tinto after its stock did well in London and oil company Woodside Petroleum.
Rio Tinto stock gained 33.6 cents to A$22.89 while Woodside shares finished 73.7 cents higher at A$11.207.
Dealers could offer no explanation for Woodside's performance and said the buying was steady throughout the day with no stand-out transactions.
After the close, a number of large parcels of Burns Philp stock were put through the market by brokerage, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell at a price of A$2.50 a share.
Dealers speculated the shares were bought by New Zealand investor Graeme Hart who bought a 14.9 percent stake in the troubled food group earlier this month.
In other markets, the short end of the Australian bond yield curve came under pressure following a strong Japanese economic report and as concerns grew over next week's Reserve Bank board meeting.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.06 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The Australian dollar sagged against the yen on Wednesday as key Japanese economic data proved so unexpectedly upbeat they could just herald the first policy tightening since August 1990.
This prospect may have helped keep the dollar steady at US$0.7511/16 by 5.35 p.m (0735 GMT) from an early US$0.7501/06.
